videos.script: Three interfaces carry most of the data in a Java program. List, Set and Map. Each one has more than one class behind it, and the classes are not interchangeable. {{lists}} It starts with the two lists. The same hundred thousand numbers, the same two operations. One list does each in a millisecond or two, and the other takes seconds. {{sets}} Then sets, which keep each element once. Three of them, three different orders, and one class that forgot half of a contract and lost track of its own books. {{maps}} Then maps, and three methods that turn a page of checking into one line each. {{choosing}} Last, how to choose. Not by habit, but by the question the program asks most often. By the end you can name the collection a problem needs before you write the first line.
